item.title: Capcom has a plan for when its rollout of Resident Evil remakes eventually catches up with newer games in the series, and considers Resident Evil 7 as a "turning point."
item.description:
Capcom has a plan for when its rollout of Resident Evil remakes eventually catches up with newer games in the series, and considers Resident Evil 7 as a "turning point."
That's according to Jun Takeuchi, a Capcom veteran who has served as excutive producer for the series over the past decade, who has acknowledged the fact that Capcom's hugely popular remakes are slowly running out of classic games to re-release. The publisher has already remade Resident Evil 2, 3 and 4 to great success, with a new version of Code Veronica slated for next year.
It has previously been reported that a Resident Evil 0 remake will follow in 2028, and that a Resident Evil 1 remake has also been considered. Of the mainline Resident Evil games, this would then just leave Resident Evil 5 and 6 as the only titles left to get new versions — both of which would be interesting prospects, for separate reasons.
While Capcom likely has enough remakes to keep their releases going for another decade, there will come a point where the publisher needs to decide whether to remake other titles, or start remaking its remakes all over again. Or... do something else, Takeuchi teased.
"The current Resident Evil series is being developed along two tracks," Takeuchi noted, writing in the just-released Biohazard 30th anniversary special magazine book now available in Japan (thanks, RENews_X, via The Gamer).
"Someday, the remake series will catch up with the era of the numbered titles, and we are already thinking about what we will do when that happens," he continued. "In fact, we have been gradually preparing for that since around Resident Evil Village. The appearance of names such as Umbrella and Spencer, as well as the return of Raccoon City in Requiem, are also in preparation for a 'crossover'.
"At first, we included these elements with the sense that they were fan service, but users were far more delighted by them than we had imagined, and they even began analysing the thoughts that the development team had privately kept to itself. So, as a series, we decided to respond to users' expectations and pushed this setup further in Village and Requiem."
Takeuchi went on to state that Capcom regarded Resident Evil 7 "as a turning point for the series" as it was in development when its plans to start remaking older games really came to fruition. Does this mean that everything before 7 is set to be remade one day, while 7 and onwards is considered too new?
Resident Evil 5 sold hugely well, with particular interest in the game in the wake of the top-rated Resident Evil 4. (Sadly, 5 was nowhere near as good.) But any new version of the game would see Capcom returning to the controversy over 5's African setting and companion character Sheva. As for Resident Evil 6, which featured a range of protagonists, it just isn't very good. But perhaps Capcom could salvage it in an eventual new version?
What's more interesting here is Capcom's suggestion that is using its remakes to seed ideas it will pick up again in newer titles, when that "crossover" point eventually happens. After all, Resident Evil has now been going for 30 years, which is a long time for anyone to remember plot details without being able to revisit early entries.
For now, though, all of that is a long time off — and there's plenty to look forward to. The promising-looking Resident Evil Veronica is next on the docket, and we've already asked Capcom some of our burning questions...
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Microsoft’s high-profile deal for Hideo Kojima’s Physint is reportedly “substantially below what Xbox would typically spend to develop a premium game.”
item.description:
Microsoft’s high-profile deal for Hideo Kojima’s Physint is reportedly “substantially below what Xbox would typically spend to develop a premium game.”
Xbox snapped up Physint after Kojima pitched the game to new CEO Asha Sharma — a pitch Kojima conducted after Sony canceled the previously PlayStation-exclusive project. For more on that, check out IGN’s recent interview with Hideo Kojima himself, where he talks through how he found out Sony had ditched Physint, and his concern about the fate of Kojima Productions.
Since then, there have been a number of online reports about the budget for Physint, with some claiming the deal was around $400 million. Subsequent reports claimed the figure was substantially less. Now, in a New York Times profile of Sharma, it was reported that Xbox may have negotiated a deal for less than you’d expect for what is expected to be a full price, triple-A spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid from the creator of the franchise.
Here’s the relevant blurb from the NYT article:
After hours of diplomatic conversation about her competitors, Sharma had a rare moment of speechlessness when discussing the deal for Kojima’s upcoming stealth game Physint. She laughed at the idea of apologizing to Sony before shrugging and saying she was happy Kojima chose to work with Xbox.
The agreement was substantially below what Xbox would typically spend to develop a premium game, according to people close to the agreement, and included film and TV rights. Sharma also clarified that work with Sony would continue: “Competition and collaboration can coexist.”
Xbox’s deal for Physint includes adaptations (Death Stranding is getting exactly that). Kojima told IGN that Microsoft was “not thinking of just funding a game. They're thinking about movies and anime. It's more about the IP. Let's create a new IP. And that's bigger in scale, so to speak. And not many other game publishers or game developers have that kind of vision.”
So, whatever the exact figure, we know Xbox is funding Physint the project, not just the video game. So we might see a Physint live-action movie (will it go up against the Metal Gear Solid movie?!), potentially an anime, and maybe even more.
Video game production budgets have risen dramatically in recent years, especially in the west where development costs have skyrocketed. Triple-A video game sales haven’t risen to match these rising costs, putting pressure on the triple-A video game industry.
In the wake of Physint’s move to Xbox, Bloomberg reported that Sony had concerns around the success of Death Stranding, as well as Physint’s development timeline, budget, and platform strategy. Kojima Productions issued a statement in response, although it failed to directly address Bloomberg’s reporting.
“Make no mistake, this was a serious situation for the studio with a range of potentially significant implications,” Kojima Productions said. “While we recognise that the article may have caused alarm, we want to reassure you all, for the record: that the studio is in a healthy, profitable state, development for Physint continues to move forward with Xbox, and our relationship with PlayStation remains strong.​”
Physint remains without a release window. It is expected after the launch of OD, Kojima's next video game for Xbox.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: October's PlayStation Plus monthly games lineup has been officially revealed by Sony.
item.description:
October's PlayStation Plus monthly games lineup has been officially revealed by Sony.
This month's trio of titles include a slightly out of date racer, a monster-filled extraction shooter, and a multiplayer voxel shooter. Let's dive in.
Launched last year, F1 25 is the actually pretty good entry in Codemasters' long-running Formula 1 racing series that we awarded with an 8/10. "F1 25 is a far broader and better package than last year’s installment, and it’s comfortably the strongest the series has been since the fan favourite F1 2020," we wrote in IGN's F1 25 review.
Next up, Hunt: Showdown 1896, Crytek's first-person extraction shooter that sends you off to fight mythological monsters. Originally launched in early acces back in 2018, when we awarded the game a 7.5/10 in our Hunt: Showdown 1896 review, this PS5 version also features a battle royale offering. And don't worry if you haven't played the first 1895 games in the series, you'll soon pick it up.
Finally, Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2 is available for PS4 and PS5. This third-person shooter with local and online co-op tells the story of what happened to the voxelEarth after the events of the first installment. Brothers from across the world reunite to face an unprecedented threat brought about by an all-new enemy that threatens to tear the Earth apart all over again.
PlayStation Plus Extra/Premium:
So, anything you fancy?

item.title: Pirates of the Caribbean actor Geoffrey Rush has said he's keen to make a return to Disney's swashbuckling franchise, if only to "annoy Jack Sparrow" one last time.
item.description:
Pirates of the Caribbean actor Geoffrey Rush has said he's keen to make a return to Disney's swashbuckling franchise, if only to "annoy Jack Sparrow" one last time.
Rush is one of just three actors to appear in all five Pirates of the Caribbean movies, alongside Johnny Depp's Captain Jack Sparrow and Kevin McNally's loyal first mate Gibbs. And while we don't know yet which characters are set to return for Disney's long-awaited sixth blockbuster, all signs point to several classic characters being brought back.
Of course, Rush's character Hector Barbossa died in the finale of 2016's Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales, the franchise's final film to date. But even this would not necessarily stop him from returning, Rush believes.
"There's been a big enough break," Rush told Entertainment Weekly, discussing his desire to return. "I said, you know, I sacrificed myself for my daughter, I don't want it to be too easy and too cheesy that I come back and go: 'give me another payday.' I respect the scale of the opera that's almost been created in that 20 year period.
"I liken it to... Shakespeare," Rush continued, "and Hamlet's father coming back as a ghost. I thought, that would take good writing but just to come back and annoy Jack Sparrow for one more go. I'd even say, get the fans to write in what they'd like to see happen."
Back in August, Pirates of the Caribbean producer Jerry Bruckheimer said he was now talking with Depp about his own potential return to the franchise, despite previous comments by the actor that made such a return seem extremely unlikely, as Disney mulled other, alternative routes forward for the franchise. Depp's past legal issues with ex-wife Amber Heard saw Disney largely distance itself from the star, leading to some choice words from Depp in response.
Long-gestating plans have placed Barbie star Margot Robbie at the forefront of Pirates 6 if and when it does ever materialize. That said, Bruckheimer has previously confirmed his intent that "some" previous Pirates of the Caribbean actors would return for the next movie, while also offering "a new take" on the franchise overall. Depp, meanwhile, appears to have retained a strong affection for his role as Jack Sparrow, which is widely seen as his most popular character among his fans. Fellow Pirates star Orlando Bloom has strongly hinted he wants to see Depp back, as well. Could Rush also follow? Get writing those letters.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Pokémon Pokopia has revealed what players can expect from its first Halloween-themed event, “Pumpkaboo’s Sweet Surprises.”
item.description:
Pokémon Pokopia has revealed what players can expect from its first Halloween-themed event, “Pumpkaboo’s Sweet Surprises.”
The limited-time event will run from 5am on October 17 until November 1, based on your Switch 2 system’s clock. (Looking at you, time travelers.) Pumpkaboo’s Sweet Surprises will follow a similar structure to previous events, featuring new Pokémon, decorations, and habitats, which require players to get their hands on a new currency: candy.
As the event’s title suggests, Pumpkaboo will be the star of Pokopia’s Halloween show. Starting on October 17, players will be able to start the event by talking to the dual-type Pokémon outside of finished Town Centers. Pumpkaboo will have plenty of new spooky items to trade, but he'll ask for some pumpkin candy in exchange.
We don't know the exact lineup of new items being added to the game, but promotional images show Jack-O-Lanterns, spooky trees, and a glowing ghost decoration.
How do you collect the candy to get these items? Well, players will need to have at least started the Bleak Beach area to get Zorua’s Camouflage ability. During the event, players will be able to use Camouflage to play tricks on their Pokémon, turning into their favorite items and then surprising them with their true Ditto form. Yep, your Pokémon will reward you for scaring and disappointing them.
Like previous events, some of the new Halloween-themed items can be used to build a new habitat. This time around, players can work toward building the habitat for Pumpkaboo’s evolution, Gourgeist. Both Pokémon will hang around after the event ends, giving players the chance to permanently add some spookier Ghost-types to their Pokopia areas.
We've had nothing but praise for Pokopia since it first launched, highlighting its "surprisingly deep world" in our original 9/10 review. With the cadence of updates, that world seems to just keep getting bigger. The previous in-game event, Fetching Scales for Feeba, was released soon after the massive 2.0 update and Bubbly Basin DLC.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: Diablo 5 game director Joe Shely has suggested a return to more methodical gameplay.
item.description:
Diablo 5 is still a couple of years away, but that hasn't stopped the speculation on how the game will actually play. People certainly expect a lot of elements from Diablo 3 and 4 to carry over to the new game, but Game Director Joe Shely has suggested a return to more methodical gameplay.
Seemingly in response to the video Path of Exile's Chris Wilson released about Diablo 5, Shely took to Twitter where he promised "while Diablo 5 will continue to feature some DEX (moment-to-moment execution) mechanics, on balance the game will be an INT/STR game (planning and investment)."
While Diablo V will continue to feature some DEX (moment-to-moment execution) mechanics, on balance the game will be an INT/STR game (planning and investment). We are designing to the core tenet of ARPGs that any challenge can be overcome with the right build.
There has been a lot of discussion around Blizzard invoking Diablo 2 when debuting Diablo 5 at Blizzcon, and how the team needs to shift away from the modern itemization and game design of the last few Diablo games to make that happen. According to Shely's post, it seems like Diablo 5 is heading in that direction. We'll just have to wait and see if Diablo 5's moment-to-moment gameplay is meaningfully different from Diablo 4's focus on infinitely scaling content that you clear in seconds. However, the community seems skeptical.
Over on Reddit, the top comment from user /u/Steve_Cage is simply "they said all this before 🤣🤣," and the top reply to that one is from /u/Tragedy_Boner who said "They ALL say this. And when the game comes out most people want to blast and not be methodical. No modern ARPG ever stays slow." Some people seem to think that even if this is the goal from the start, Blizzard will reverse course after launch. User /u/Usernameasteriks says "They won’t follow through, if they even try in the first place. Once the first wave of people complaining they can’t blast through content quickly they will restructure it all."
On Twitter, though, people seem a little more optimistic. User Dagon5 replied with "I'm happy to hear this. Honestly this is an opportunity to try the other direction from what D3/D4 was trying to accomplish. Just go all in on itemization depth etc, and skill systems." And that certainly seems like what Shely is setting out to accomplilsh.
I've personally never had a problem with Diablo 4's approach to itemization, and I like jumping in and seeing just how far I can push in the Pit each season. But, I also jump back to Diablo and Diablo 2 occasionally when I want to play something that focuses more on creative itemization. Luckily, even if Diablo 5 does lean towards Diablo 2's way of doing things, it sounds like the team will keep adding new seasons to Diablo 4 after launch, so you can always just stick with that game.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: Peacock has officially announced Ted: The Animated Series, with Seth MacFarlane, Mark Wahlberg, and Amanda Seyfried returning to voice their original roles.
item.description:
Peacock announced Wednesday that TED: The Animated Series will premiere with eight episodes on December 17, with additional episodes set to stream in 2027.
Created by Seth MacFarlane, Paul Corrigan, and Brad Walsh, the cartoon is a sequel to the two live-action Ted movies. You can check out the teaser trailer here and find the new poster below.
The animated series brings back the cast of 2012’s Ted and 2015’s Ted 2.
MacFarlane reprises his role as the voice of Ted; Mark Wahlberg, as the voice of Ted's best friend, John; Amanda Seyfried, as the voice of John's wife, Sam; and Jessica Barth as Ted's wife, Tami-Lynn.
Kyle Mooney and Liz Richman also join the cast as series regulars in the roles of Apollo and Ruth, respectively.
“Picking up twelve years after the conclusion of the last movie, John and his thunder-buddy Ted are neighbors, both with families of their own and dead-end jobs,” according to the official plot synopsis.
“Follow these two lovable stoners as they enable each other's bad ideas about marriage, parenting and the challenges of adult life.”
Corrigan and Walsh serve as co-showrunners. Rough Draft Studios, Inc. animates the show.
McFarlane and Peacock previously teamed for two seasons of the live-action Ted: The TV Series.
McFarlane recently cast doubt on Peacock greenlighting Season 3 given the costly visual effects involved in bringing his foul-mouthed teddy bear character to life.

item.title: Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has offered new Xbox CEO some words of advice as she resets Microsoft’s gaming business: “pick a lane.”
item.description:
Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has offered new Xbox CEO some words of advice as she resets Microsoft’s gaming business: “pick a lane.”
In an interview with The Expansion Pass, the former boss of Sony Interactive Entertainment America called the decision Asha Sharma now faces Xbox’s “Dreamcast moment.”
This is a reference to Sega’s earth-shattering exit from the console business following the commercial failure of the Dreamcast. That call, made early 2001, ended a run of console manufacturing that included the likes of the Sega Genesis, Game Gear, and Sega Saturn. Sega instead focused on releasing video games on previously rival consoles, such as Sony's PS2.
Fast forward 25 years, and Xbox is in the middle of a dramatic restructure that has already seen nearly 2,000 staff lose their jobs, multiple studios either exit Xbox or face closure, and various games canceled. Xbox is now focused on fewer, bigger video game franchises such as The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and Minecraft, with the likes of Halo moved over to Call of Duty company Activision. Through it all, there are question marks hanging over the viability of Xbox’s confirmed next-gen console, Project Helix.
With this in mind, Layden was asked if he had any advice for Sharma, having led a video game business of his own. He presented two options: go hard on taking on PlayStation now and in the future, with the assumed launch of Project Helix and PlayStation 6, or pack up those console plans and focus on software.
“You got to pick a lane,” he began. “Either you're going to be a platform competitive with PlayStation — which Xbox has not been competitive with PlayStation for years — but that's not out of the window. You know, you can still make another run at it. And there are certain decisions you have to make around that about the platform. We talked about exclusivity. We talked about, how do you incentivize third-parties to support your platform in a meaningful way? This is all things around the platform business.
“Or you sit back and realize you are the biggest game publisher in the world. Well maybe Tencent’s bigger, but in the Western world you are the biggest game publisher out there with Activision and Blizzard and Bethesda and all the other pieces. Be that. This is your Dreamcast moment, when Sega decided we're just going to be on PS2 and we're going to get out of the hardware business and just be a great software company. It can be done. It's been done before. So, that's my advice. Pick a lane.”
Microsoft has for years now fended off questions over whether it plans to exit the console hardware business amid poor sales of Xbox Series X and S and, before it, Xbox One. Publicly, Microsoft boss Satya Nadella and Asha Sharma have remained committed to console hardware, with Sharma saying it’s central to the company’s gaming plans. But Sharma has also said in recent months that Microsoft needs to think carefully about how Xbox consoles work and make money, particularly with the RAMpocalypse driving up prices.
In June, Sharma said the spiralling cost of new and existing consoles would require "radically different business models" over the coming generation. Speaking to Fortune, Sharma acknowledged the increasing price of existing hardware and components — fuelled by global crises and the rise of AI — and said the industry had "reached a point where it will be hard to imagine" mass audiences still being able to afford "thousands of dollars" for a new console generation.
And just this week, former PlayStation executive Shuhei Yoshida said Sony and Nintendo needed to make their current consoles last as long as possible amid soaring costs that have already prompted PS5 and Switch 2 price rises.
Big questions remain. What, exactly, does Project Helix look like? How far down the exclusivity road will Xbox go? And here’s the biggest of all: will Xbox eventually exit the console business?
Photographer: Patrick T. Fallon/Bloomberg via Getty Images.

item.title: Nintendo will launch a physical Switch 2 version of Pokémon Legends: Z-A with its Mega Dimension DLC bundled in.
item.description:
Nintendo will launch a physical Switch 2 version of Pokémon Legends: Z-A with its Mega Dimension DLC bundled in.
The complete version of the game will launch on cartridge this October 29, The Pokémon Company confirmed today. This will include the shinier version of the game playable on Nintendo Switch 2 (though this cartridge can also be played on Switch, if you want to buy now and upgrade your hardware later).
Mega Dimension is, of course, the expansion for Pokémon Legends: Z-A that allows players to go on further adventures in Lumiose City via new portals created by Hoopa. Key features here are the ability to temporarily control Pokémon at levels greater than 100, and encounter even more Mega Evolutions — such as Darkrai, Magearna and Baxcalibur.
While Mega Dimension launched last October as a separate download, this combined package means that anyone purchasing Pokémon Legends: Z-A this holiday will be able to get the complete game in one go. You'll also unlock a gift of 100 Ultra Balls to get your catching off to an ultra start.
Nintendo has no major new Pokémon game due this holiday, so a re-release of Pokémon Legends: Z-A makes sense. There's still some time to go until the next generation of Pokémon games arrives next year, exclusively for Switch 2, in the shape of Pokémon Winds and Pokémon Waves.
But could there be one other surprise before the end of the year? Some fans are convinced that re-releases of Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald will also launch in 2026, though we'll have to wait and see if these become a reality.
"Pokémon Legends: Z-A finally feels like Game Freak hitting its stride in Pokémon's 3D era," IGN wrote in our Pokémon Legends Z-A review, awarding the game an 8/10 score. "Lumiose City may not be visually exciting, but exciting Pokémon encounters, well-written characters, and amusing side quests still make it fun to explore."
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Marvel fans need to prepare for "a very surprising ending" to Avengers: Doomsday, directors Joe and Anthony Russo have teased.
item.description:
Marvel fans need to prepare for "a very surprising ending" to Avengers: Doomsday, directors Joe and Anthony Russo have teased.
Speaking to Fandango, Anthony Russo described the upcoming Marvel blockbuster as a "focused propulsive narrative," while still weighing in as one of the studio's longest films to date.
As you might expect from a movie with such a large cast, Avengers: Doomsday will clock in around the "two-and-half hour" mark, though even the Russos are unlikely to know the exact runtime just yet as reshoots were believed to be taking place only this month to add even more material.
Only three Marvel movies have ever stretched longer than two-and-a-half hours (150 minutes), with the appropriately named Eternals at an everlasting 157 minutes, Black Panther: Wakanda takes Forever at 161 minutes, and Avengers never Endgame at a whopping three hours and one minute (or 181 minutes total).
Still, Anthony Russo suggested Avengers: Doomsday audiences wouldn't be bored.
"It's a two-and-a-half hour movie or so, and you're sitting through it, and it's a focused propulsive narrative that has an organizing principle at its center, and everything has to orbit around that," he said. "That's part of the creative challenge for Joe and I — just figuring out what that orbit is and how it all smashes together."
As for how it all concludes — and leads into next year's climactic Avengers: Secret Wars — the Russo brothers had this to say:
"I think people are going to be surprised," Joe Russo teased. "It's a very surprising ending. It's a very surprising movie and that's all we'll say about it."
What could this mean? Well, with Doomsday being just part one of the story, it seems clear the movie will not end Doctor Doom's story just yet, and therefore it seems extremely unlikely the film will wrap everything up with a happy ending.
Even without knowledge of the Secret Wars comics or informed speculation based on filming leaks and reports, it seems fair to compare Doomsday to Infinity War, the first film in the Russo brothers' previous Avengers two-parter. That movie ended with the Avengers losing to Thanos, with multiple main character deaths throughout the film that were not reversed, then a climactic event that acted as a shocking cliffhanger. Will the Avengers lose again to Doctor Doom? I would not describe this as too surprising, but it would certainly serve as an interesting jumping off point for Secret Wars, should it follow the Marvel comics' general story.
The Russos have been doing the rounds promoting Avengers: Endgame Encore, which features four brand new scenes they have confirmed won't appear in Doomsday itself. One of these scenes sees Doom "collect" the Hulk, potentially suggesting he will sit out Doomsday and return in Secret Wars. Avengers: Doomsday launches in theaters on December 18.

item.title: Here's every animal revealed for GTA 6 so far, now that Rockstar has confirmed the game features an incredible 170 species.
item.description:
Here's every animal revealed for GTA 6, now that Rockstar has confirmed the game features an incredible 170 species.
Yesterday's big blowout of new GTA 6 information revealed via Game Informer included Rockstar putting a number on the zoo-sized menagerie of creatures set to feature within its upcoming blockbuster — including 60 birds, more than 30 land mammals, and a variety of fish and reptiles. Also, we got confirmation that the game will actually feature at least one zoo for you to visit.
“Florida has a diverse animal ecosystem that we wanted to faithfully include across the different biomes in Leonida – urban and rural environs, aquatic life both inland and ocean, and the wetland habitats like the swamps and Everglades,” Rockstar vice president of dynamic art, Michael Kane, told Game Informer.
“The animal art and population teams are incredibly passionate about delivering animals that are accurately researched and look visually correct in every respect, alongside the supporting movement and animation to bring them to life.”
With that in mind, now seemed a great time to list every animal we have personally spotted so far, based on Rockstar's trailers, the Extended Look, and every single screenshot released to date, as well as confirmed sightings by those who have had a chance to preview a near-final build of the game, and of course what Rockstar has confirmed.
While we've tried to be exhaustive, there are still plenty of species that Rockstar is deliberately keeping under wraps (our list contains around 50 animals, so less than a third of the final total).
There's also plenty of speculation online around what else may be included in the full game, based on their appearance in prior Rockstar games or even past leaks for GTA 6 — but we've left these species out as they remain unconfirmed for now. (Sorry, possum fans — no doubt your time will come. And no, we're not 100% on that rat sillhouette, so we haven't included that either.)
Think you've spotted something we haven't, or have a particular animal you want to see included? Let us know in the comments below!
GTA 6 features plenty more than animals, of course, and we've got extensive coverage on IGN. Check out IGN's interview with Rockstar Games, our GTA 6 preview, and word of the first confirmed GTA 6 voice actor.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: With no official word that 28 Years Later Part 3 is in the works, director Danny Boyle has chimed in to insist it will be made eventually, and Cillian Murphy will play a key role.
item.description:
With no official word that 28 Years Later Part 3 is in the works, director Danny Boyle has chimed in to insist it will be made eventually, and Cillian Murphy will play a key role.
In December last year, Sony confirmed it was moving forward with the third installment of the 28 Years Later trilogy a month before the release of the second movie, The Bone Temple. Elden Ring director Alex Garland, who wrote all the franchise entries thus far, was said to be working on the third entry, which does not have a title at this point. Danny Boyle has been open about wanting to direct it.
However, The Bone Temple flopped at the box office, casting doubt on the sequel. Now, amid continued radio silence from Sony, some fans fear the trilogy will never be completed.
But speaking at Zurich Film Festival (as reported by Variety), Boyle issued a positive update, although Sony has yet to rubber stamp it.
“28 Years 3, or whatever it ends up being called, will get made because people keep asking about it,” Boyle said. “Quite when I’m not sure, but there’s a script — a very good script by Alex Garland.
“[It will have] a lot of Cillian Murphy in it. Whether he’ll take his kit off anymore, that I don’t know. He’s got the Oscar now.”
The Bone Temple hit theaters in January 2026, just over half a year after 28 Years Later enjoyed box office success. Despite great review scores (IGN’s review returned an 8/10), The Bone Temple made only $58.5 million worldwide — just over a third of 28 Years Later’s $151 million.
In a May interview with Empire, The Bone Temple director Nia DaCosta expressed surprise with the theatrical results. “It’s so funny, because literally every barometer we use in the industry to determine whether or not a movie is good, and people like it and want to see it, was through the roof, and yet our box office wasn’t there,” DaCosta said. “I made a great film, and I’m really proud of it, and people liked it.”
DaCosta suggested there may be some truth to the suggestion that The Bone Temple came out too soon after 28 Years Later, causing audience confusion. “People were like, ‘Oh yeah, I saw that last summer!’ I’m like, ‘No, no, so there’s a sequel!’”
In March, Murphy said he was keen to finish the trilogy following his cameo in The Bone Temple. But despite Murphy and Boyle all wanting 28 Years 3 to get made, and Garland's script ready and waiting, we all know it will be Sony that makes the call.
While you wait to find out, check out IGN's article, 5 Questions We Have For the Next 28 Years Later Movie Following The Bone Temple.

item.title: Horror movie legend John Carpenter has slammed the 2011 The Thing prequel movie, calling it a “piece of crap.” But not all his fans are onboard with his take.
item.description:
Horror movie legend John Carpenter has slammed the 2011 The Thing prequel movie, calling it a “piece of crap.” But not all his fans are onboard with his take.
2011’s The Thing serves as a direct prequel to Carpenter’s much-loved 1982 horror masterpiece, The Thing. It revolves around a team of Norwegian scientists who discover a parasitic alien buried deep in the ice at a Norwegian Antarctic research station. Directed by Matthijs van Heijningen Jr. and written by Eric Heisserer, The Thing flopped at the box office, grossing just $31.5 million worldwide. It has a 34% rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes’ Tomatometer, and a 43% rating from fans.
IGN's own The Thing review returned a 5/10. We said: "The special effects quickly devolve into over-the-top goriness, with some of the Thing's forms coming across as more ludicrous than terrifying. There are some risible CG moments involving the morphing of actors' faces with the creature's, and the whole last act falls apart into a 'chase the CG bogey monster before it gets you' sequence devoid of any true suspense or originality."
Count the 78-year-old Carpenter as one of The Thing's fiercest critics. During a recent panel at FanExpo in Chicago, Carpenter pulled no punches when discussing the movie. “They made a sequel, I guess, or something,” he began. “Norwegian camp — did you see that piece of crap? They did digital effects and they had… Instead of a blood test it was a dental test. I mean, it was unreal. It’s like, what?! The dentist?!”
Kurt Russell, who starred in Carpenter’s The Thing and joined him on the panel, responded to Carpenter’s comments to say, “John doesn’t suffer fools greatly guys.”
While most agree 2011’s The Thing isn’t the best movie in the world, some fans have come to its defense in the wake of Carpenter’s outburst. “To be fair to the creators of The Thing (2011), it wasn’t their fault that the movie became a ‘piece of crap,’” one fan said.
“Director Matthijs van Heijningen Jr. and the creature effects team at Amalgamated Dynamics had created a ton of practical creature effects for the film. However, the studio and production ultimately decided that the practical effects looked too ‘dated’ and too much like an 80s movie, so they chose to replace most of them with CGI. Even the director later admitted that, in hindsight, it was the wrong decision from the studio.
“No offense to John Carpenter, but if you’re going to blame anyone for how the 2011 movie turned out, blame the studio.
“There are also workprints featuring the original practical creature effects stored in the studio vaults. Fans have been calling for these to be released and remastered, restoring the original practical effects so we can finally see the movie closer to how it was originally intended.”
“I honestly liked it and appreciated how respectful it was of Carpenter’s movie,” another fan added. “It was a complete retread of The Thing, but it was pretty good actually,” one person said. “Would be way better if they didn't put CGI over top of all the practical effects.”
“Did we need it? No. Am I glad we have it? Yes,” another fan commented.
Since The Thing’s release, van Heijningen has discussed his regret about the CGI reshoots, telling Syfy Wire in 2023 that the movie was “caught in a cross-zone where animatronics were old-fashioned and the CGI wasn’t good enough.”
“We made the wrong decision to do it in post-production [when it came to] making the monster design in the computer,” he continued. “I regret that now.”
“The Carpenter version was so good and a lot of fans were almost offended by the prequel and didn’t see the necessity for a follow-up. But now I fully understand that it was a bit early.“
van Heijningen also discussed where a potential sequel would go had The Thing not bombed at the box office. "Kate would escape and would be picked up at sea and tries to warn the world at an oil platform near the South Pole," he explained. "The monster would break loose on the the rig. I liked the oil rig mayhem idea."
Alas, there’s zero chance those sequel ideas become reality, given the movie’s poor critical and commercial performance... and Carpenter’s clear disdain for it.
Photo by Daniel Boczarski/Getty Images.

item.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered can be unlocked on Switch 2 for free via any physical version of the game for Switch — whether its your copy of the game or not.
item.description:
The Witcher 3 Remastered can be unlocked on Switch 2 for free via any physical version of the game for Switch — whether its your copy of the game or not.
Switch 2 owners have discovered that physical cartridges for The Witcher 3 on Switch can be used an unlimited number of times to grant a digital copy of The Witcher 3 Remastered. So, all you need to do is rent or borrow a copy of the game to unlock unlimited access. And no, you don't need to keep the original game cartridge inserted after unlocking the upgraded digital version.
Have a friend with the game? Ask to borrow it! Have a cheap second-hand game shop nearby? Head in and see if there's a copy for sale, and then trade it back in!
This remarkably generous solution is the result of CD Projekt keeping its promise that upgrades for the newly-relaunched RPG classic will be free on all platforms, even for physical copies. And while there's no version of The Witcher 3 Remastered for Nintendo's original Switch, the game will unlock a free version of Remastered for Switch 2.
Major features added in the remaster include improvements to combat, traversal and movement, plus revamped mount handling, enhanced monster behaviors, a skill tree revamp, armor transmog, an expanded photo mode, new finishers and much more.
Other additions include the long-awaited cross-platform mod support, new quest tracking, immersive meditation, refined animations, UI improvements, a looting rework, refreshed motion blur, new accessibility features, a tutorial modernization, HDR improvements, a foliage shading rework, ray-tracing improvements, a global lighting reork, new shading model, subsurface scattering, and a new tone mapper.
Of course, all of this is coming ahead of next year's Songs of the Past, The Witcher 3's third expansion, which you will need to pay for. While that's still some time away (we don't know yet exactly when in 2027 it will arrive), The Witcher 3 Remastered is an enormous game — and remember, it also now includes the game's first two expansions as standard. So, you'd better get started.
To ease you into Geralt’s life on the road, check out the Things The Witcher 3 Doesn’t Tell You, plus IGN’s The Witcher 3 Walkthrough and The Witcher 3 Endings guide, which outlines all of the major quests and choices in the base game and expansions (now bundled in with the Remastered edition). When you’re ready for the tough choices, check out our The Witcher 3 Sex and Romance guide to see who Geralt can smooch and all the opportunities to do so. And to make Geralt as strong a monster hunter as possible, check out all the Witcher Gear Locations, Places of Power Locations, and even Gwent Card Locations.

item.title: Rockstar Games has revealed the lengths it went to to gain first-hand experience of real-life Florida as part of research for GTA 6.
item.description:
Rockstar Games has revealed the lengths it went to to gain first-hand experience of real-life Florida as part of research for GTA 6.
Senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, told Game Informer that developers at the studio visited strip clubs and rode around at night with ex-cops as part of research conducted in Miami and South Florida.
“We go and try to experience everything… from riding around areas at night with ex-cops, to going to strip clubs and nightclubs, spending time on the beach, in the Everglades, down in the Keys, and beyond,” Humphries said.
Of course, Rockstar has recreated Florida before in previous GTA games, but the last one featuring Vice City — GTA’s take on Miami — was 2006’s Vice City Stories. Unlike previous Vice City games, GTA 6 is set in the modern day, and things have obviously changed over the last 20 years.
GTA 6 gameplay and screenshots have already teased how the game will adapt Florida, known as Leonida in-game. The GTA 6 map has six different regions: Vice City, of course; Leonida Keys; Grassrivers; Port Gellhorn; Ambrosia; and Mount Kalaga National Park. Activities include kayaking, street and off-road racing, and air boating. We’ve also seen nightclub gameplay, beach gameplay, and plenty more.
The elephant in the room here is the strip clubs, which were featured in a high-profile GTA 6 gameplay leak that also showed off a nudist town filled with naked characters. Male and female genitalia were both fully exposed in the leaked gameplay, but it’s worth pointing out this was unofficial footage, and Rockstar hasn’t released official strip club gameplay yet. It may not do so before launch.
None of this should be particularly surprising, given this is GTA 6 we’re talking about. Most of the GTA games feature strip clubs, although not all are open for players to visit. GTA 6, clearly, takes this to another level, as it does with most gameplay features seen in previous entries.
We’ve rounded up all the major new details from Game Informer’s GTA 6 cover reveal, and we have plenty more on the game from IGN’s trip to Rockstar North last month. GTA 6 launches in November on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S.

item.title: Nicolas Cage has issued his verdict on the Marvel Cinematic Universe, calling it a "well-funded and glorified WWE," despite its use of top-tier acting talent.
item.description:
Nicolas Cage has issued his verdict on the Marvel Cinematic Universe, calling it a "well-funded and glorified WWE," despite its use of top-tier acting talent.
Speaking at Fan Expo Dallas, Cage aired his thoughts on Hollywood's largest-grossing franchise of all time — despite his own participation in a slew of comic book movie projects.
"I do say this with love," Cage began. "When I see these 50-plus, otherwise intelligent, remarkably gifted thespians putting on these ridiculous outfits and getting ready for the fight — and let's face it, it's cutting all to the fight — it's hard for me not to be reminded that the MCU is becoming a well-funded and glorified WWE."
On the one hand, you could argue that Cage's heavy involvement in comic book projects offers him a unique perspective on the matter. On the other, Cage has worn plenty of ridiculous outfits himself.
As detailed in IGN's own guide to all of Cage's comic book TV and movie projects, the actor is famous for starring in Ghost Rider and its sequel Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance, and Big Daddy in the original Kick-Ass. Infamously, Cage was also set to play Superman in Tim Burton's scrapped Superman Lives — though did ultimately cameo as Kal-El in an episode of The Flash.
In animation, Cage voiced Superman in Teen Titans GO! To the Movies, Dr. Tenma in Astro Boy, and of course voiced Spider-Man Noir in Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, a role he reprised for this year's live-action Spider-Noir — a role Cage recently spoke positively of.
So, what's going on here? Is Cage finally tired of superhero projects, or is he just being a bit Nicolas Cage about it all? Regardless, it seems best not to raise your hopes too high for him to make a surprise appearance in Avengers: Secret Wars, which will surely feature a ridiculous outfit or two.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Valve has issued a huge update to its in-development MOBA hero shooter Deadlock, propelling it to the top of Steam’s most-played games chart.
item.description:
Valve has issued a huge update to its in-development MOBA hero shooter Deadlock, propelling it to the top of Steam’s most-played games chart.
The update significantly updated the map, added six new heroes, new mobs, objectives, updated the HUD, healthbars, the Shop, and much more. Valve has updated the Deadlock engine code to the latest version of Source 2, improved anti-cheat, prediction improvements, rendering performance, audio performance, item art, and added new SFX for all hero Heavy and Light Melee. There's loads more to this update, detailed on the Deadlock website.
Deadlock hit a concurrent peak of over 220,000 players overnight, smashing its all-time concurrent peak and making it the sixth most-played game on Steam last night. Deadlock remains in early development, and access is limited to friend invites via Valve’s playtesters, so the concurrent peak is truly impressive.
In a post on Steam, Valve issued an update on Deadlock development, and pointed to future updates. It said it’s working on large item redesigns and additions, and even alternate game modes “that expand the scope of the game,” although there’s no guarantee either makes it into the final launch version.
Other future updates will focus on Midboss (both the model and the layout to a degree), Guardians and Walkers, “which we do consider important but just haven't gotten to yet and will be focusing on.” Hero remodels sound like they will be done later in the process, but we might see some of that work in upcoming updates.
There is still no word on a release date or even a release window for Deadlock, nor when the game will be expanded with a beta. It remains a game that Valve is working on while it continues to support other big hitters such as Counter-Strike 2 (easily the biggest game on Steam even now), Dota 2 (easily the second-biggest game on Steam, even now), and, occasionally, Team Fortress 2 (which remains one of the most-played games on Steam, even now). Based on the interest in Deadlock even at this stage, it looks like Valve will have another Steam hit on its hands when it eventually does come out.
And no, there isn’t a whiff of Half-Life 3 anywhere right now.

item.title: Warner Bros. has posted a social media ad highlighting the deeply divided critical response to Tom Cruise and director Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s new film Digger just hours after the review embargo was lifted.
item.description:
Well, that was fast. Warner Bros. has posted a social media ad highlighting the deeply divided critical response to Tom Cruise and director Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s new film Digger just hours after the review embargo was lifted.
As of writing, the movie, which opens in theaters October 2, has a “rotten” score of 52% on review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes and a score of 44 on Metacritic. (Cruise’s lowest-rated film on Rotten Tomatoes is Cocktail with 11%.)
As Entertainment Weekly reports:
“The ad begins with a quote from X user @thejonathansim: ‘Digger is an ambitious film sure to polarize audiences.’ It then cuts to a clip from the film featuring Cruise’s Digger Rockwell saying, ‘You know what? F--- those people!’ The rest of the ad shows positive and negative phrases from various reactions to the film flipping back and forth on screen including ‘unpleasant’ and ‘masterpiece,’ ‘baffling’ and ‘brilliant,’ and ‘insufferable’ and ‘magnificent’.”
IGN’s Michael Calabro was on the mixed side in his Digger review, awarding the film an “okay” score of 6 out of 10:
“Digger's satire may not change your thinking on global warming, but there are excellent performances and more than a few laughs… Digger is far from a must-watch, and if the trailer has you feeling skeptical, save your money. The theater experience won't change your mind, and the laughs that are there still will be when it hits HBO Max.”
Billed as “a comedy of catastrophic proportions,” the satire stars a nearly unrecognizable Tom Cruise as tycoon Digger Rockwell, whose oil drilling operations spark a global disaster.
Digger opens in theaters October 2.

item.title: Diablo 4 director Brent Gibson is telling fans not to worry about the game after Diablo 5’s announcement sparked concerns about the former title’s lifespan.
item.description:
Diablo 4 director Brent Gibson is telling fans not to worry about the game after Diablo 5’s announcement sparked concerns about the former title’s lifespan.
Diablo 5’s reveal at Blizzcon 2026 left fans equal parts excited and worried. Of course, players were pumped for a new Diablo game — but with Diablo 4 having just launched in 2023, the reveal of a new game so soon felt like a death knell for the one they were still playing.
But Brent Gibson, director of Diablo 4, says there’s nothing to fuss about. Speaking with Icy Veins, Gibson outlined some plans for the game’s future content, saying it will continue to receive support well after 5’s release.
“I have an analogy,” he began. “If you’re wearing a sign in the middle of Times Square saying, ‘The end is nigh,’ the end is not nigh. We have a lot coming. We have [the] Amazon [class] coming down the road. The train isn’t stopping.
“One of the things I love about our world is we are not a series of games. We are a universe. We are even adding to Diablo 2 with the Warlock. It’s one of the few franchises where we have the luxury of continued play, and we know our communities.
“If you’re worried, don’t sweat it, because we’re going to be making content for a long time. But we are excited about Diablo 5. We’ve got a show coming. Gone are the years of waiting a decade for more content. It’s a great place to be.”
More specifically, Gibson said Blizzard is planning on supporting seasons for Diablo 4 “as long as the community continues to show up” for it, specifically mentioning the ongoing support for Diablo 2 and Diablo 3.
“There are still people who play those games, and as long as you’re showing up, we’re going to continue to be making content," he assured.
As Gibson mentioned, Diablo 4 is getting the Amazon class in the first half of 2027. With three more years to go until Diablo 5 is released, there’s still plenty of time for developers to flesh out the title with even more classes and experiences — something they spoke about during a dedicated Diablo panel at Blizzcon this year.
“Diablo 4 has bright support,” Diablo 5 director Joe Shely said. “It's fully supported by the team. We were just announcing earlier today, coming to Diablo 4, the Amazon, the Season of Hell's legacy, Diablo 4 is coming to Switch 2, and there will continue to be ongoing support for Diablo 4. There's many reasons for players to keep playing.”
“We have dedicated teams for each of those games because those games are important to us and they're really important for our community,” production director Tiffany Wat added. “I think it really gives us a really great opportunity to be able to collaborate together, to talk with one another. Even though we might be distinct teams, we still work together quite closely because ultimately we are making games for the Diablo community. I think it's the best time to be a Diablo fan.”
For more Diablo news, you can check out our interview with the developers here, as well as catch up with their reaction to the series' animated show coming to Netflix.

item.title: David Jaffe, the creator, co-writer, and director for the original God of War game, has cleared up his viral comments about Ariel Lawrence, creative director for Laufey.
item.description:
David Jaffe, the creator, co-writer, and director for the original God of War game, has cleared up his viral comments about Ariel Lawrence, creative director for Laufey.
Ariel Lawrence has been with the God of War franchise since its very first game — but creator David Jaffe, who left the series behind in 2007 to form his own studio, says he never got along with her during his time at Santa Monica Studio.
He described their contentious work relationship in a September 2026 live stream while reacting to footage for God of War Laufey, where he claimed their personalities clashed and that he didn’t feel as though she was truly passionate about the games they were making.
“I have no problem with female directors at all,” he began. “This woman started as an assistant producer back when we were making the first God of War. Her and I never got along. She thought I was kind of obnoxious and I thought she was pretentious. She didn’t put the audience first.
“People that I didn’t get along with on God of War were people, in my opinion, who were more about, ‘I wanna do well in the corporate world… I want to play the game,’ versus, ‘I’m here with a vision and I will f**kin’ fight you for that vision.’ There was a lack of passion I felt from her, and she was also kind of a judgy asshole, to me.”
Jaffe also slammed Cory Barlog for making Laufey in the first place — which he called a “stupid” game — and asked why he couldn’t “sit Ariel down and say, ‘This isn’t ready.’”
pic.twitter.com/xkPvif83KY
Jaffe’s comments unsurprisingly went viral, sparking a debate within the God of War fanbase and the broader gaming community in general. Not long afterward, Jaffe took to Twitter/X to expound upon his remarks, where he called out those using his statement to harass Lawrence online.
“Look, I personally didn't like Ariel and I don't THINK she cared much for me back when we worked together. Oil and Water, just very different types of people. And honestly, she was probably more liked on the team than I was. You see, if you haven't noticed, I can be, as my ex-wife says, 'a lot,’” he wrote.
“And so in this video, I was responding/sharing that aspect of our time working together. That's the only way I would ever talk about former colleagues, be it good or bad experiences. For people to use my experience with Ariel as an excuse/launching pad to make personal attacks on her is just low and s**tty.
"She's a real person — just like you — with a life and feelings and people who care for her and who love her, and it just seems really f**king cruel to do that. Plus, have you looked in your own mirror? I've looked in mine; that s**t's scary! You see this f**king beard?!? Good lord, I'm days away from moving to the North Pole…”
Look, I personally didn't like Ariel and I don't THINK she cared much for me back when we worked together. Oil and Water, just very different types of people. And honestly, she was probably more liked on the team than I was. You see, if you haven't noticed, I can be, as my… https://t.co/kw0g4JGnMf
Laufey has, unfortunately, been a target for the online rage machine, and Jaffe's remarks are adding more fuel to the fire. Trolls’ remarks about Deborah Ann Woll’s appearance and their outrage over the fact that a woman is leading a God of War game totally overwhelmed gaming circles on social media when it was first revealed in June, and this finger-pointing doesn’t appear to have stopped, but rather simply slowed down.
Other games have since taken the brunt of the internet’s apparent boredom, as evidenced by the debate surrounding Insomniac’s Wolverine. But still, Laufey has managed to catch strays in this regard, with The Last of Us director Bruce Straley using it as an example of why modern AAA games no longer “excite” him (though he later apologized for this comment).
God of War Laufey releases on February 16, 2027, exclusively for PlayStation 5.
